text:
caroline: quick heads-up — rankpro-v1-ptq results are weird on curated-bench: MRR +4.7% but NDCG@10 -2.9% vs fp16. putting raw numbers and notes below for triage.
ton y: hmm MRR up and NDCG down usually means top1 improved but tail got worse. did retrieval pool change?
caroline: possible — our preproc pipeline for this run applied title-dedupe (new dedupe step) at candidate curation. command I ran: 
```bash
python -m eval_harness.run --model rankpro-v1-ptq --dataset curated-bench --pool_strategy top200 --dedupe_titles True --seed 7 --workers 64
```
rachel: raw baseline (fp16) vs ptq:
- fp16: MRR=0.312, NDCG@10=0.489
- ptq : MRR=0.327, NDCG@10=0.475
rachel: pooled size distribution: median_pool_fp16=198, median_pool_ptq=73 (because dedupe collapsed many candidates)
tom: that explains a lot. MRR benefits if duplicate near-top items consolidate (boosting top1), while NDCG suffers because overall ranked diversity shrinks — fewer unique relevant items across positions.
caroline: ran a quick ablation: same model but dedupe_titles=False -> NDCG@10=0.488, MRR=0.325 (MRR still up vs fp16, NDCG near baseline).
tony: so the metric delta is primarily a curation artifact, not model semantics. good catch. we should quantify significance though. did you bootstrap?
sree: i ran bootstrap 10k samples on query-level scores:
- delta MRR = +0.015 (95% CI [0.009, 0.024])
- delta NDCG@10 = -0.014 (95% CI [-0.024, -0.006])
sree: both are significant. but split by cohort: short queries (<8 tokens) show MRR gain larger, long context queries show NDCG drop larger.
rachel: sample outputs: i dumped top10 ranks for 10 queries where NDCG drop is largest and shared CSV at https://internal.redwood/charts/rankpro/5489990000 (view-only).
caroline: thanks. actionables I'm proposing: 1) re-run eval with fp16 retrieval + ptq rerank (to isolate retriever effect), 2) run with full_pool (no top-k prune) and no dedupe, 3) add pool_size histogram to eval portal so we surface this automatically.
ton y: also add NDCG@1/3/5/10 reporting. MRR alone hides position effects.
tom: small experiment idea: compute normalized diversity metric (unique_ids_in_top10 / 10) per query and correlate with NDCG delta. that should quantify dedupe impact.
sree: i'll run the bootstrap per-slice for those runs and post CI. scheduling three jobs: 
- job A: fp16-retriever + ptq-rerank, dedupe=True
- job B: fp16-retriever + ptq-rerank, dedupe=False
- job C: same as B but pool_strategy full
infra-bot: eval job queued: A=5490000100, B=5490000200, C=5490000300. estimated walltime ~3h each. logs will be in /eval-results/5490000*/.
caroline: nice. also small note: ensure candidate dedupe uses canonical_id (not title) for deduplication; title normalization is brittle (HTML, punctuation).
ton y: agree. policy: dedupe should be optional and tagged in run metadata. add `run_metadata.dedupe_method` to harness output.
rachel: i'll PR a dashboard change to show pool_size and dedupe_method. linking draft: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/pr/1221
tom: one more sanity check: run on prod-sampled-1m to ensure this isn't dataset-specific.
sree: queued prod-sampled-1m as job D=5490000400 after A/B/C.
caroline: thanks team. if A (fp16 retriever + ptq rerank dedupe=True) still shows NDCG down, then model changed ranking beyond pool effects and we need deeper logit-level diffs. otherwise we'll blame curation and update onboarding docs.
ton y: cool. marking ownership: caroline will verify A/B/C results and open a follow-up issue with CSV of top-10 mismatches. sree owns the bootstrap/CI. rachel owns dashboard PR. tom will prototype the diversity vs NDCG correlation.
caroline: will post results here when jobs finish. :eyes:
